notes: Correct in both backends, with root-at-symlink support and NewObject agreement; the symlink-only special case in zip Open is an odd ad-hoc addition, and zip counts skipped links outside the root; tests are comprehensive, including copy and escape.

Code matches the reference exactly: lazy zip reads, squashfs readlink via StatT, name-consistent newObjectNative and clamped link Open; adds sensible docs plus squashfs, zip and end-to-end escape tests, though range/seek and NewObject-agreement coverage is thin.

Works and shares a tidy OpenLink helper, but zip eagerly decompresses every symlink member with an unbounded io.ReadAll at mount time (memory/latency risk for hostile or S3-hosted archives), and squashfs NewObject swallows real errors into ErrorObjectNotFound; tests are thorough.
Identical to C2: reference-equivalent implementation with docs and reasonable tests covering skipping, translation, regular .rclonelink files and the hostile-archive copy.

Squashfs symlink objects store no target and Open tries a nonexistent .rclonelink path, readSymlink reads through sqfs.Open and silently swallows panics, NewObject without the suffix still returns symlinks, and the skip log is Infof (not a notice) on a racy sticky field; the escape test does not test the real attack.

Correct for both zip and squashfs, with List/NewObject agreement, regular .rclonelink files kept and single-file roots working; the squashfs NewObject/New logic is more convoluted than needed, link Open errors on an offset past the end, and the in-process squashfs test uses a global os.Chdir.

Functionally sound for both backends with List/NewObject agreement and a defensive filter for children of symlinks under --links, but it relies on an untyped Readlink interface, clamps offsets for all zip objects, and accidentally deletes an existing test's doc comment.

Zip appends the suffix after root matching, so a root naming link.rclonelink is not found; it drops members beneath symlinks even without --links; squashfs adds a ReadDir walk over every path component on each List/NewObject, a heavy-handed escape defence that also changes semantics.
